data.narrative:
Telexistence, a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Jin Tomioka and Ken Tomoyose, has raised over $170M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 9 private and 1 public company operating in the same sector and stage, including peers Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, Divergent, and Exotec.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression approach used total raised ($170M) as a proxy for post-money valuation and applied a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yielding $323M. The peer-median method examined three same-sector, same-stage comparables with valuations ranging from $1.6B to $2.0B (Dexterity, Bedrock Robotics, and Generalist AI), producing a median implied value of $1.8B. This wide dispersion reflects heterogeneity in the robotics space regarding commercialization progress and capital efficiency.

Synthesizing these methods produces a valuation range of $275M to $2.0B, with a median of $1.0B. The stage-progression method yields the lower bound, relying on historical raise data and a mechanistic multiplier. The peer median anchors the upper range but carries meaningful uncertainty given the small sample size and diverse business models within the comparables. Key uncertainties include Telexistence's revenue, path to profitability, and competitive positioning relative to the peer set. Additional clarity on customer traction and burn rate would narrow the range materially.
